- search_property(text, limit=10) -> (total_matches, [{'pid':'P..', 'label':.., 'lang':..}]). Finds a PROPERTY by name in any of the six languages: exact matches first, then prefixes, then substrings. 1 read.

Not a dict — it has no .items(). value_type is one of 'wikibase-entityid' (value is a QID), 'string', 'time', 'quantity' — those four spellings and no others. The default keeps preferred statements when present, otherwise non-deprecated ones; all_ranks=True returns every statement. This rank filter can hide many values: to enumerate everything a node LINKS to, use edges(), which applies no rank filter.
- references(qid, pid=None) -> LIST of {'property': 'P..', 'property_label':.., 'value':.., 'sources': [{'property':.., 'property_label':.., 'value':..}]}. Only sourced statements appear; a statement absent from this list is unsourced.

- label(qid, lang) -> one label without language fallback
- descriptions(qid) -> descriptions in the six target languages
- edges(qid, direction='both', pid=None, limit=None) -> outgoing and incoming graph edges as {'out': [...], 'in_': [...], ...}. Use this BEFORE a sweep: degree() reports a node's total across every predicate, which is the wrong number for one predicate. Then page the sweep with edges(qid, direction=.., pid=.., limit=L, offset=K) — offset skips the first K MATCHING edges, so successive pages cover the set exactly once. A pool or 'reviewed' field is the count of the candidate set the question describes, not the size of your answer.
